originality.rationale: The mathematical statement classifies all generic central-plane section side counts, including both facet-type counts, of the two nonregular convex quasiregular polyhedra. Matteo (arxiv:1403.2125) establishes the object classification, while the geometrically closest inspected exposition (Freire) discusses rectangular vertex figures and special equatorial hexagons/decagons but does not state the generic octagon/dodecagon law. The old statements do not quantify the generic normal domain or give the chamber-invariance proof. No equivalent theorem was located in the web and semantic record searches, with acknowledged historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: This supplies an exact all-orientation section complexity classification for the complete nonregular convex quasiregular 3-polyhedron class, including triangle/square and triangle/pentagon face incidences, a reusable local balance criterion and affine stability. It resolves a geometrically motivated distinction between generic sections and famous special equatorial hexagonal/decagonal cuts. Unlike testing an arbitrary finite sample or textbook edge counts, it proves a structural rigidity property for continuum many planes.
